ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a schematic diagram of longitude and latitude lines; the central horizontal line is labeled 0°, indicating the equator; there are multiple vertical meridians in the figure; in the upper right there is a longitude scale labeled "90°"; the dashed line is an inclined terminator line and intersects a meridian at the equator. Place A is located on a meridian east of this intersection. Estimated according to the proportion of the 90° longitude scale at the top of the figure, the meridian where place A is located is about 45° east of the meridian where the terminator line intersects the equator. Then reason: the question stem explains that the shaded and non-shaded parts represent two different dates; combined with the position of the date boundary, it can be judged that the dashed line in the figure corresponds to the dusk line. The local time at the dusk line on the equator is 18:00. Place A is about 45° east of that point, and local time increases by 1 hour for every 15° eastward, so the increase is 45°÷15°=3 hours. 18:00+3 hours=21:00. Therefore the local time at place A is 21:00.
